references.text: The crowd repeats its cry to crucify Jesus and release Barabbas: [ref:Luk 23:21|Luke 23:21].
Matthew's parallel account where the crowd is persuaded to ask for Barabbas and demand Jesus be put to death: [ref:Matt 27:20-21|Matthew 27:20-21].
The crowd cries out, "Crucify him!" in Matthew's account: [ref:Matt 27:22-23|Matthew 27:22-23].
Mark's parallel account where the people ask for Barabbas to be released instead of Jesus: [ref:Mark 15:11-14|Mark 15:11-14].
John's account where the crowd shouts that they want Barabbas released and not Jesus: [ref:Joh 18:40|John 18:40].
The crowd cries out, "Away with him! Away with him! Crucify him!" – the same expression "Αἶρε" is used: [ref:Joh 19:15|John 19:15].
Peter reminds the people that they denied the Holy and Righteous One and asked to have a murderer set free – a direct reference to choosing Barabbas over Jesus: [ref:Apg 3:14|Acts 3:14].
Paul refers to how the people in Jerusalem asked Pilate to have Jesus executed, even though they found no guilt in him: [ref:Apg 13:28|Acts 13:28].
Luke explains who Barabbas was – one who had been thrown into prison for rebellion and murder: [ref:Luk 23:19|Luke 23:19].
Isaiah prophesies that the Lord's suffering servant would be despised and rejected by people – fulfilled when the crowd rejected Jesus in favor of a criminal: [ref:Jes 53:3|Isaiah 53:3].
